_doc: Curated technique ontology (knowledge_architecture.md section 5): mechanism, preconditions (predicate DSL), predicted metric directions (up | down | flat | up_or_flat | down_or_flat, on canonical metrics), realizations by scope (target:<key> | target:<backend>:sm_NN+ | target:<backend> | family:<name> | universal). 'aliases' are v1 / technique-DB / footer names folded into the entry. 'states' gates a technique to state chains (empty: any state); 'op_classes' to op classes (empty: any); 'slot': offered by the multi-slot agent. Techniques of the old JSON DB and the footers that are not folded in here are imported by ontology.seed_legacy() with slot=false.

techniques.mechanism: consecutive lanes touch consecutive addresses, so every memory transaction carries only useful bytes
risks: a transposed mapping can break coalescing of the other operand

realizations.how: Make consecutive threads (work-items) touch consecutive addresses; reorder the thread->element mapping, transposing through on-chip memory when the natural mapping is strided.
Keep the unit-stride dimension innermost so vector loads are vle (unit stride), not vlse (strided).

techniques.mechanism: wider loads and stores per instruction: fewer memory instructions and more bytes in flight per lane
risks: misaligned base pointers or sizes not divisible by the vector width

realizations.how: Use float4/float2 (half2 for fp16) loads and stores where alignment and sizes allow; keep a scalar tail.
Use vload4/vstore4 (float4, half8) where alignment allows; keep a scalar tail.
Strip-mine with vsetvli at LMUL=m4/m8 and vle32/vse32 so each instruction moves VLEN*LMUL bits.

techniques.mechanism: block / grid shape matched to the machine: enough resident warps and full waves, no idle tail
risks: more threads per block can cut registers per thread and spill

realizations.how: Choose block size / grid shape for occupancy and to cover small problems; use grid-stride loops so the grid matches the SM count.
Tune the work-group size to a multiple of the wave size (64 on Adreno) and the global size to fill every SP.

techniques.mechanism: several independent operations per thread so the scheduler can issue while earlier ones wait on memory or the pipeline

realizations.how: Unroll inner loops (#pragma unroll) and give each thread several independent elements / accumulators to hide latency.
Unroll 4-8x with independent accumulators; in-order cores have no OoO to hide the load-use bubble.

techniques.mechanism: declare inputs non-aliasing and read-only so loads can be reordered, batched and served from the read-only cache path

realizations.how: Mark inputs const __restrict__ and use __ldg for read-only data.
Mark inputs __global const restrict; use image2d_t reads (texture cache) for read-heavy 2D data on Adreno.

techniques.mechanism: stage a reused block in fast on-chip memory so each DRAM element is read once per tile instead of once per use

realizations.how: Tile the operands through __shared__ memory (e.g. 32x32 or 64x64 tiles), __syncthreads() per k-step, so each element is read from DRAM once per tile.
__shared__ tiles filled with cp.async in a 2-3 stage pipeline (cuda::memcpy_async / __pipeline_memcpy_async).
Tile through __local memory with barrier(CLK_LOCAL_MEM_FENCE) per k-step.
Block loops so each block's working set stays L1-resident; strip-mine the inner loop at VLEN.

techniques.mechanism: each thread computes a TMxTN block of outputs in registers, reusing every loaded operand TM or TN times
risks: spills when TMxTN is too large

realizations.how: Each thread computes a small TMxTN block of outputs in registers (outer-product micro-kernel over the k loop).
Keep a 4x4 (or LMUL-wide) accumulator block in registers across the reduction; write back once.

techniques.mechanism: load the next tile while computing the current one, overlapping memory latency with arithmetic

realizations.how: Prefetch the next shared-memory tile into registers (or a second buffer) while computing the current one.
cp.async into a second shared buffer with cp.async.wait_group; compute on the other.
async_work_group_copy the next tile into a second __local buffer, wait_group_events before use.
Software-pipeline: issue loads for iteration k+1 before the FMAs of iteration k; __builtin_prefetch 64-128 elements ahead.

techniques.mechanism: treat the convolution as a GEMM (M=N*OH*OW, N=OC, K=IC*KH*KW) without materialising im2col, so GEMM blocking applies

realizations.how: Treat the convolution as a GEMM (M=N*OH*OW, N=OC, K=IC*KH*KW) without materialising im2col; tile it like a GEMM.
im2col into an L1-sized buffer, then the vectorised GEMM micro-kernel.

techniques.mechanism: reduce in registers across the lanes of a warp, with no shared-memory round trips or barriers per step

realizations.how: Reduce within a warp with __shfl_down_sync, then across warps via shared memory.
sub_group_reduce_add / sub_group_reduce_max (cl_khr_subgroups), then across subgroups via __local.

techniques.mechanism: split one serial accumulation chain into independent partial sums combined at the end: depth N -> log N

realizations.how: vfredosum.vs / vfredusum.vs in-vector reductions over K independent partial sums.
Block-level tree reduction in on-chip memory, one partial per thread first.

techniques.mechanism: map one block (or warp) to each reduced row and parallelise the reduced dimension, so every lane has work

realizations.how: Map one block (or warp / subgroup) to each reduced row; parallelise the reduction dimension across its threads.

techniques.mechanism: fewer passes over memory and fewer kernels: compute statistics and output in one sweep

realizations.how: Compute statistics and the normalised output in as few passes over memory (and as few kernels) as possible.
Fuse the passes into one loop nest so intermediates stay in vector registers.

techniques.mechanism: a grid sized to the machine, each thread looping over wide elements: full bandwidth with minimal index math and launch cost

realizations.how: Grid-stride loop with float4 accesses; minimal integer math per element.
Global size = a few waves per SP, each work-item loops over vload4 elements.

techniques.mechanism: precompute strides and divisions; fewer integer divides and multiplies per element

realizations.how: Precompute strides/divisions outside the loop; use fewer integer divides per element (iterate the inner index, carry the outer).

techniques.mechanism: tile Q/K/V through fast memory with an online softmax so the score matrix never round-trips through DRAM

realizations.how: Tile Q/K/V through shared/local memory with an online softmax so the score matrix is never materialised.

techniques.mechanism: matrix units execute a whole 16x16xK multiply-accumulate per instruction, far above the scalar FMA ceiling

realizations.how: nvcuda::wmma 16x16x16 fragments (fp16 inputs, fp32 accumulators); for fp32 problems only if the tolerance allows rounding inputs to fp16.
mma.sync with tf32 or bf16 inputs and fp32 accumulators (wmma::precision::tf32 for fp32 tensors).

techniques.mechanism: pad or swizzle shared-memory rows so a warp's accesses hit distinct banks instead of serialising

realizations.how: Pad shared/local tiles by one element per row (e.g. [32][33]) or XOR-swizzle the column index so lanes hit distinct banks.

techniques.mechanism: fewer, fatter threads: amortise index math and reuse operands across several outputs per thread
risks: too few threads for small problems

realizations.how: Give each thread 2-8 outputs (along the contiguous dimension), reusing loaded inputs and index math across them.

techniques.mechanism: split the reduction (K) dimension across blocks when the output is too small to fill the machine
risks: an extra reduction pass / atomics; atomics change rounding order

realizations.how: Split K across blocks (grid.z); each writes a partial tile, then a second small kernel (or atomicAdd) sums them.

techniques.mechanism: one launch covers many instances or iterations, so per-launch overhead is paid once

realizations.how: Persistent kernel or CUDA graph over the instances; merge back-to-back kernels.

techniques.mechanism: cheaper instructions for transcendentals and divisions (intrinsics, polynomial approximations)

realizations.how: Use __expf/__logf/__fdividef/rsqrtf intrinsics where the tolerance allows; avoid double-precision literals.
native_exp / native_divide / half_ intrinsics where the tolerance allows.
Degree-4 minimax polynomial after range reduction instead of libm expf/tanhf.

techniques.mechanism: fewer live registers per thread so more warps are resident to hide latency

realizations.how: __launch_bounds__(threads, minBlocks), narrower live ranges, recompute cheap values instead of keeping them.

techniques.mechanism: less on-chip memory per block (reuse buffers, right-sized dynamic allocation) so more blocks are resident

realizations.how: extern __shared__ sized per launch; reuse one buffer across phases; smaller tiles when occupancy is the limit.

techniques.mechanism: uniform control flow across a warp (predication, sorting work, hoisting bounds checks) so no lanes idle

realizations.how: Hoist bounds checks out of inner loops (interior/edge split), use predicated selects instead of divergent branches.

techniques.mechanism: less total work: a different algorithm, avoiding redundant computation or data movement

realizations.how: Remove redundant work: precompute shared sub-expressions, avoid recomputing reductions, exploit structure (separability, sparsity) in the op.

techniques.mechanism: half the bytes per element and twice the arithmetic rate on fp16 paths

realizations.how: half2 loads and __hfma2-free fp32 math: widen with __half22float2, compute in fp32, store half2.
vload_half4 / half8 loads with fp32 math (cl_khr_fp16).

techniques.mechanism: order work so blocks that share operands run close in time and hit in L2 instead of DRAM

realizations.how: Swizzle the block index (grouped/raster order) so concurrently running blocks share A/B tiles in L2.
